column3: The Hebrew says he caused his son to pass through the fire; BSB explicitly describes this as sacrificing him.
The Hebrew says the Edomites came to Elath and settled there; BSB says Rezin sent them there.
The Hebrew calls the payment a bribe; BSB calls it a gift.
The Hebrew repeats the king of Assyria and makes Damascus itself the object of deportation; BSB uses he and explicitly supplies its people.
The Hebrew repeats Uriah the priest and Damascus; BSB uses he for the second Uriah reference and leaves the return location implicit.
The Hebrew names the king three times and the altar twice; BSB uses pronouns after their first mention.
The Hebrew refers to the basin in the singular and a pavement of stones; BSB specifies a basin from each stand and describes the pavement as a stone base.
The Hebrew uses one verb for both the Sabbath structure and the outer royal entrance; BSB uses separate removing and closing verbs.
